audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed across the layers. full read Malzahar, Malzahar, Skill, Skill, Malzahar, Skill, Skill; content win[] read Skill, Skill, Malzahar, Skill, Ekko, Ekko, Ekko; and several content whys[] contradicted their own row — whys[0] 'free lane control from minute one' under a Skill row, whys[4] 'his suppress-combo one-shot threat range is simply scarier than your ult' under an Ekko row.
audit.why: The kit resolves it. Void Shift gives damage reduction and CC immunity until he is hit, and Void Swarm is 8 seconds, so he owns levels 1-3 outright. Levels 4-5 even out because Ekko's 1075 Q outranges Call of the Void's 900. Level 6 is his: Nether Grasp is point-and-click suppression, and a suppressed Ekko cannot cast Chronobreak. Only 2+ items is clearly Ekko's.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Malzahar, Malzahar, Malzahar, Skill, Malzahar, Skill, Ekko, proposed as matched pairs on every row that moves, with whys rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as a spike without the cooldown that makes it survivable.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 and only 80s at rank 3 — the longest cooldown in the lane and the entire basis for when Ekko is allowed to step forward.
audit.corrected: 140/110/80 written into spikes[1].text, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.feeding and phases[6].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither of the two interactions that actually decide this matchup appeared anywhere: Call of the Void's silence and Malefic Visions' execute threshold. wants.you[1] also told the reader to buy Merc Treads against the suppress.
audit.why: Call of the Void silences on a flat 6s at 900 range — a silenced Ekko has neither Phase Dive nor Chronobreak, which is why pre-casting E is fatal here. Malefic Visions is a damage-over-time with a threshold kill, so the health bar lies. Tenacity does not shorten suppression, so Merc Treads is not the answer to Nether Grasp.
audit.corrected: Silence written into dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[1].d, the execute into dontsFull[0].d, and wants.you[1] corrected to say tenacity does nothing against suppression.

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Void Shift gives him damage reduction and CC immunity until he takes a hit — level 1 poke barely dents.

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: Voidlings on an 8s W shove the wave for him — you are preserving CS, not looking for a level 2 trade.

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: His level 3 is Malefic Visions on 11s — 650 range of damage over time you cannot walk out of.

edits.before: Chronobreak online — your aggression gets a save file. Trade like the rewind exists, because it does.
edits.after: His 6 beats yours: Nether Grasp is point-and-click suppression and you cannot cast Chronobreak through it.

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive the carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Late you flank: Nether Grasp is 80s at rank 3, so make him spend it on someone else and Chronobreak the rest.

edits.before: Levels 4-5: still his lane — Voidling pressure plus E zone denies your window to punish.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out: your 1075 Q outranges his 900, and Voidlings die to the return pass.

edits.before: Malefic Visions plus Nether Grasp lets him delete you from range the moment he hits 6, well before your own R matters much.
edits.after: Malefic Visions plus Nether Grasp lets him delete you from 700 range the moment he hits 6, and the suppression is 140s at rank 1.

edits.before: Buy MR/Merc Treads early to blunt his true-damage-ish DoT and suppress burst
edits.after: Buy Merc Treads and MR early, but know tenacity does nothing against suppression

edits.before: Malzahar wins by landing Nether Grasp, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Malzahar wins by suppressing you point-and-click inside 700 while Void Shift ignores whatever you opened with.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your R Chronobreak like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp: 140s at rank 1, 80s at rank 3 — point-and-click suppression, so never step up solo while it is up. - Call of the Void silences every 6s. - Malefic Visions is 11s at rank 1. - Chronobreak is 110s: kill windows only, never waves.

edits.before: First item onward, trade like the rewind exists: dive the chipped, W the peel, R the answer. Your tempo compounds.
edits.after: First item onward, punish the push — his W is 8s of Voidlings but he stands still to cast, and E only reaches 650.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared push that crashes while your hologram bank stays healthy — tempo with insurance. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down — no blink, no string, no business being there. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-cleared push that crashes while your hologram bank stays healthy — tempo with insurance. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down — his Voidlings shove it back at you and Nether Grasp waits. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.

edits.before: If Malzahar takes first blood, tighten up: Nether Grasp is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q passes and stay relevant through W stuns and R picks.
edits.after: If Malzahar takes first blood, tighten up: Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1, so count it and never step inside 700 while it is up. Farm with Q passes from 1075 and stay relevant through W stuns and R picks, not duels.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry through insured dives — but Chronobreak cannot be cast while suppressed, so make him spend R first.

edits.before: You are the pick that survives the response: dive their carry, Chronobreak the collapse, and W-stun the chase that follows you out.
edits.after: Late you are the pick that survives, but only after his 80s Nether Grasp lands on someone else — then dive and Chronobreak out.

edits.before: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 and suppresses on point-and-click — until it is spent, every step you take inside 700 is his choice, not yours.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Never step in with E down — Call of the Void silences on 6s and a silenced Ekko has neither the blink nor the rewind.

edits.before: That’s Malzahar’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Malefic Visions kills at a threshold — watch the number, not the bar.

edits.before: The rewind heals off the hologram's path — diving away from your own past is how Ekkos die with R up.
edits.after: Call of the Void silences on a 6s cooldown at 900 range — silenced means no Q, no E, no rewind.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 — hoard it past the fight and you paid 100 mana for a button you never pressed.
